# Nayasamuṭṭhāna (Ne 36)

**ID:** Ne 36  
**Section:** Netti (ne)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Nayasamuṭṭhāna  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nayasamuṭṭhāna* ("Molding of the Five Guidelines") constitutes the third major subsection of the explanatory section (*Paṭiniddesavāra*) of the *Nettippakaraṇa* [Caudron 2000; von Hinüber 1996]. The section presents and systematizes the five interpretive guidelines (*naya*)—namely *sīhavikīḷita*, *tipukkhala*, *nandiyāvatta*, *disālocanā*, and *aṅkusa*—which together with the sixteen modes (*hāra*) form the core hermeneutical method of the text [Balasooriya et al. 1980; Lopez 1988; Caudron 2000; Sen 2014]. In this section, each method incorporates verses from the preceding summary section, mapping basic root terms (*mūlapada*) to their doctrinal meanings and ultimate purpose, such as leading different types of audiences to liberation [Balasooriya et al. 1980; von Hinüber 1996; Sen 2014]. Specifically, *sīhavikīḷita*, *tipukkhala*, and *nandiyāvatta* structure mappings across sets of four, three, and two terms, while *disālocanā* establishes conceptual equivalences between unprofitable and profitable terms (representing suffering and the path), and *aṅkusa* operates horizontally [Sen 2014]. Oskar von Hinüber notes that the term *samuṭṭhāna* draws on Vinaya terminology and observes that the sequence and selection of *mūlapadas* here differ loosely from those listed in the earlier *Niddesavāra*, being illustrated directly through suttanta quotations [von Hinüber 1996].

**Sources**

- [Sen 2014] Tansen Sen (ed.), Buddhism across Asia: Networks of Material, Intellectual and Cultural Exchange, Vol. 1 (2014) — Detailed analysis of the guidelines (naya), term mappings, and comparison with Gāndhārī commentaries
- [Balasooriya et al. 1980] Somaratna Balasooriya et al. (eds.), Buddhist Studies in Honour of Walpola Rahula (1980) — Context of Nayasamuṭṭhāna within the hermeneutical method of the Netti
- [Lopez 1988] Donald S. Lopez, Jr. (ed.), Buddhist Hermeneutics (1988) — Outline of the basic hermeneutical categories and root terms in Netti
- [Caudron 2000] Marian Winston Caudron, Guide to Skillful Means: Reexamining the Netti-Pakaraṇa's Modes and Methods (2000) — Structural location within the Paṭiniddesavāra section of the Netti
- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Textual composition, treatment of mūlapadas, and Vinaya linguistic parallels
- [Nakamura 1980] Hajime Nakamura, Indian Buddhism: A Survey with Bibliographical Notes (1980) — Note on Japanese translation of the Nayasamuṭṭhāna chapter
